source_user: Write a small, dependency-light Python implementation for duplicate detector. Variant 1. Contract: Detect the first duplicate request ID in a stream while preserving input order. Include tests for boundary cases and a brief complexity analysis.
source_assistant: Provide typed or clearly documented code, input validation, deterministic tests, and explicit assumptions. Contract to satisfy: Detect the first duplicate request ID in a stream while preserving input order.
corrected_answer: Implement a dependency-light pure function such as first_duplicate_id(ids) that scans request IDs in arrival order and returns the ID at the second occurrence of the earliest repeated value, or None when no duplicate exists. Define the input contract: accept an iterable of hashable request IDs, do not reorder it, and either reject unhashable or otherwise invalid values with a documented TypeError or use a clearly specified normalization—never silently coerce. A set of seen IDs gives O(n) expected time and O(u) auxiliary space for n inputs and u distinct IDs; a stream iterator is consumed once. Test empty and one-item streams, all-unique input, an immediate duplicate, duplicates after other unique IDs, three occurrences (the second occurrence wins), duplicate values of different types if supported, unhashable input, and a generator to verify order and single-pass behavior. Treat an absent duplicate as a normal None result and do not log or echo sensitive request identifiers by default.
